corrections.originalRuling: C (the tree is the architecture, over the machine contract) — src/modules/ plus three composition points already make a file's location answer "may I import this".
corrections.correctedRuling: B (machine contract over any layout). C is the recorded target, blocked on the canary WG-ARCH-006 must produce. The src/modules/ move already made stands as an unproven move, not as warrant for C.
corrections.why:
Apply the three branches of the decision rule in order. (1) "Agents in the workforce or a second consumer of any shared layer: at least B, from the first week." Agents write this code — CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md exist as the agent entry point. Branch fires; the floor is B. (2) "Move to C when a canary exists that proves moves are output-neutral, and do the move in one reviewed change." I grepped tests/ and src/ for toMatchSnapshot, toMatchInlineSnapshot, toHaveScreenshot, __snapshots__, golden and characterisation: zero hits, zero snapshot directories. No build-output hash either — the only createHash under tests/ is fs-helpers-hash.test.ts, a unit test of a hash helper. The C branch's stated precondition is FALSE, and the wargame's "It depends on" names it verbatim: "Whether a proof of harmless movement exists (tests or an output canary)." (3) "A is acceptable only for a single-surface S venture" — PatterStage is M. Decision rule output: B. Default agrees: "B, rising to C once a canary exists."

How the original was flattery: C is the single option that requires PatterStage to do nothing, because ADR-0005 already made the move. The walk read the artefact as the warrant. The doctrine grades the proof, not the directory — both worked rulings it cites reached C by building the canary FIRST and moving second (PatterTech_Business ADR-0001 then ADR-0007, "both hashes unchanged after the re-shape"). PatterStage moved first and proved nothing. The tree stands; the grade does not. Note the walk's own WG-ARCH-006 ruling concedes the canary is absent, so two rulings in one batch contradicted each other.

B is also not met, so this is not a downgrade to something free. design-lint runs inside `npm run lint` and carries three boundary rules. Two are true contracts at zero — I read the baseline and neither core-imports-no-module nor module-registry-stays-pure appears in it. The third, hermes-outside-adapter, is baselined at 21 crossings across 13 files (src/app/page.tsx, GatewayBanner.tsx, VersionFooter.tsx, ModelEditor.tsx, five API route handlers, src/lib/deploy-spawn.ts, src/lib/db/profiles-tools-parity-ensure.ts, two config pages). A shrink-only counter stops the 22nd crossing; it does not make the 21 a contract. B's own words are "the layering fails the build when crossed" and "the contract file documents the architecture." A number documents nothing.
corrections.note: B, machine contract: two of design-lint's three boundary rules are clean contracts, hermes-outside-adapter's 21 baselined crossings are not; C stays the dated target, blocked on WG-ARCH-006's canary, which the src/modules/ move was made without.
corrections.workImplied: Name the 21 hermes-outside-adapter crossings instead of counting them: convert each baseline entry to an inline pragma carrying a written reason, or close it behind the AgentRuntime port. Record C as a dated target conditional on WG-ARCH-006's canary landing. No files move.

corrections.originalRuling: A (one shared database) — one deployable, one operator, one SQLite file; a second physical database would be pure ceremony.
corrections.correctedRuling: A with C's seam. One patterstage.db, with analytics_events and chat_messages declared the readings class — named consumer, retention window, prune path — and the physical split written now as the migration that fires if volume forces it.
corrections.why:
The decision rule's first clause: "A high-volume feed with different retention or legal weight than the core: C, and design the boundary before the feed exists." The feed exists, so the clause has already fired. 012_analytics_events.sql creates an append-only table with three indexes and no expiry column, written from 18 recordEvent() call sites across src/. 013_chat.sql adds chat_messages, append-only, holding full turn content plus reasoning and tool_calls_json. Both grow per interaction. The core — missions, schedules, models, credentials, profiles — grows per operator decision: ADR-0004's measurement of the live database records runs=22, sessions=35, missions=16 after five weeks. That is the volume asymmetry, and the retention asymmetry follows from it: the core is meant to be kept, the log is not.

I searched src/ for VACUUM, retention, prune, TTL and expires_at. The only DELETE-for-age anywhere in the app is LogSync.ts:169 keeping the most recent 500 error_log_entries. So the venture already knows how to write a prune; it has not written one for the two tables that need it.

How the original was flattery: the walk established the trigger in its own conflict paragraph and then demoted it to a footnote about "doctrine rule 7" rather than letting it change the ruling. Plain A is today's single file with zero work owed — the option that costs nothing. But plain A is not what the rule produces once the feed exists, and it is not what the precedents produce: WiseWattage is recorded as "A with C's seam", AutoWatt as "C as constitutional law... with A serving until telemetry exists." Both keep one physical store and design the boundary.

Why not full C: the reason is in the venture brief rather than invented. One file the operator can back up is the local-first promise, and a second SQLite file is a second backup story on a stranger's machine — which is also where WG-OPS-003 already found the restore path missing. Full C is not ruled out; it is deferred with its trigger written down. What is ruled out is the current position: unbounded append-only tables on a machine the operator intends to run for years, and on machines belonging to people he has never met, where the loss is not his to accept.

This ruling forces the collision with WG-ARCH-003, which is ruled in that entry: the prune cannot ship before the per-Body progression snapshot does.
corrections.note: A with C's seam: one patterstage.db, but analytics_events and chat_messages are declared readings — consumer, retention window and prune path designed now, and the split written as the migration that fires if volume forces it.
corrections.workImplied: For analytics_events and chat_messages, write the four facts the rule demands — consumer, retention window, prune path, and the migration that splits them out if volume forces it — into the migration headers and an ADR. Then implement the prune, ordered AFTER WG-ARCH-003's per-Body snapshot lands. No second database today.

corrections.originalRuling: B (raw SQL behind a repository layer) — PatterStage "already routes persistence through 16 hand-written *-repository.ts modules"; the seam is breached in three route handlers.
corrections.correctedRuling: B, and B is not met. The seam is bypassed in 19 files holding 49 prepare() sites, not the three route handlers named — and those three are the smallest, at 4 statements between them. A design-lint rule confining `.prepare(` to the repository layer and src/lib/db/ is owed, baselined at today's count and shrink-only.
corrections.why:
The option letter survives; the grade does not. Decision rule: "The service owns its schema and has any performance-shaped data (time-series, bulk writes, large reads): B." PatterStage owns all its tables (49 CREATE TABLE statements across its own migrations), carries no ORM in package.json, and has time-series-shaped data (analytics_events with three indexes, error_log_entries, run aggregates). B is what the rule produces. That part of the first walk is right.

What is wrong is the claim of compliance, and the flattery is there rather than in the letter. B's substance is stated in the option itself: "Hand-written SQL in one place, typed adapters outward... a repository seam tests can stub." I ran the count. `grep -rln "\.prepare(" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx src/ | grep -v repository` returns 31 files. Twelve are the DB plumbing itself (src/lib/db.ts, src/lib/db-schema.ts and ten appliers under src/lib/db/), which is the seam's own floor. The remaining 19 files hold 49 prepare() sites: session-sync.ts (12), stats/agent-stats.ts (5), analytics/run-aggregates.ts (4), sync/sources/ProcessSync.ts (3), seed/catalog-seed.ts (3), config-cache.ts (3), composer/seed.ts (2), mission-model-audit.ts (2), orchestration/scheduler/BackgroundScheduler.ts (2), sync/sources/SessionSync.ts (2), sync/sources/LogSync.ts (2), api-logger.ts (1), stats/agent-experience.ts (1), sync/sources/EnvSync.ts (1), sync/sources/MemorySync.ts (1), modules/hermes/lib/state-import.ts (1), plus the three route handlers at 1, 1 and 2.

The walk reported the 4 statements visible from the app router and called that the breach. They are 8% of it. Sixteen times more SQL sits outside the seam in src/lib than in the route handlers named. Two further corrections to the same line: there are 25 *-repository.ts modules, not 16; and "already routes persistence through" reads as a met ruling when a seam bypassed in 19 files is not one place.
corrections.note: B stands as the option and is unmet in fact: 19 files hold 49 prepare() sites outside the 25 repositories and the db/ plumbing, so the seam needs a shrink-only design-lint rule to become the contract B describes.
corrections.workImplied: Add a design-lint rule forbidding `.prepare(` outside src/lib/**/*repository*.ts and src/lib/db/, baselined at today's 19 files / 49 sites and shrink-only — the same mechanism the repo already runs for design-lint. One rule plus a baseline entry; it converts the seam from an aspiration into a contract and makes the 49 shrink instead of grow.

corrections.originalRuling: B (durable database claim queue) — the deterministic occurrence id with a PK guard "is B's substance on SQLite's guarantees"; the A-shaped defect is scoped to Deep Research.
corrections.correctedRuling: A with B's seam designed in — the doctrine's own default. PatterStage has B's idempotent claim and none of B's rebuildable unit: boot recovery re-fails work, it never rebuilds it, and the durability of what does survive is the Hermes backend's property, not the queue's. B is the target, promoted when the unit-builder registry exists.
corrections.why:
Option B names its components: "a jobs table claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, idempotency keys, stale-claim reaping, and a unit-builder registry (closures do not serialise; persist context, rebuild work from it)." PatterStage has the claim — tick.ts builds a deterministic occurrence id `sch_${id}_${nextRunAt}` whose PK guard rejects a duplicate tick, and recomputes due work from next_run_at rather than an in-memory timer. It has reaping of a sort (reconcileActiveRuns, failStuckResearchRuns). It has no unit-builder registry: I grepped src/ for unit-builder, unitBuilder, rebuildUnit and registerJob and nothing of the kind exists.

The consequence is in the code rather than in an argument. run-reconcile.ts's reconcileRunsOnBoot() is the whole of boot recovery: every active run without a backend id is set to "failed" with "PatterStage restarted before the run was submitted" and its mission finalised failed. The function's own header states where durability comes from for the rest — runs survive "because HTTP runs survive a CH restart", i.e. the Hermes backend holds them. That is borrowed durability and it leaves with the backend. instrumentation.ts does the matching re-fail for research (failStuckResearchRuns on boot), and composer/dispatch.ts:75 dispatches research the same fire-and-forget way (`void runResearchJob(...)`). So the defect is not Deep Research's alone as the walk scoped it: it is mission runs, composer research nodes and standalone research alike.

Apply the rule. "Jobs must survive deploys or scale on separate workers, and one database serves the system: B" — jobs here must survive a restart, since a mission run that consumed LLM spend and is thrown away is exactly the harm, against a standing "no spend without my approval." So B is the right target. But the default states what you rule while the seam exists and the queue does not: "A with B's seam designed in (idempotency keys and rebuildable units from day one); promote to B when the first job that must not vanish appears." PatterStage has half that seam and none of the rebuildable units.

How the original was flattery: crediting the claim mechanism as "B's substance" grades the venture on the component it has and stays silent on the component that decides whether a queue is durable at all — then scopes the failure to one subsystem, so the ruling implies a patch instead of a registry.
corrections.note: A with B's seam designed in: the deterministic-occurrence claim is real, the unit-builder registry is absent everywhere, and boot recovery re-fails rather than rebuilds — durability today is the Hermes backend's, not the queue's.
corrections.workImplied: Build a unit-builder registry: persist each dispatched unit's context (kind, inputs, target) at claim time, register a builder per kind, and rebuild on boot instead of re-failing. Apply it to all three dispatchers — mission runs, composer node runs and research jobs — not as a Deep Research patch. Promote the ruling to B when it exists.

corrections.originalRuling: A (always computed), with B for the config read. Note: "None on the ruling; this is the one wargame PatterStage already answers to spec."
corrections.correctedRuling: A for stats generally; C for the per-Body progression record — an immutable per-profile snapshot carrying its inputs digest, landed before any prune — because WG-ARCH-008's retention makes its inputs erasable; and B for the config read only once its invalidation owner is complete, since four in-app writers of config.yaml never invalidate.
corrections.why:
"This is the one wargame PatterStage already answers to spec" is the failure mode stated out loud. Two branches of the decision rule fail on inspection.

(1) THE C BRANCH. Rule: "Point-in-time legal or attestation weight: C, and the snapshot records its inputs so it can be re-derived and audited." The walk rejected C on "nothing here carries attestation weight." Check it. 011_drop_game_tables.sql records that the kept progression "is derived live from real activity in the stats layer, so there is no game state to persist"; derive.ts:314 computes `unlocked: current >= def.target` on every read; its inputs are analytics_events lifetime aggregates — analytics-repository's distinctActiveDays() scans `SELECT DISTINCT date(created_at) FROM analytics_events ORDER BY d` over the whole table, distinctEventTypeCount() runs `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT event_type)` over the whole table. Standing alone, A is fine while nothing erases the inputs. But WG-ARCH-008 now rules retention onto exactly those tables, and the day a prune ships the operator's level drops and unlocked achievements un-earn. ADR-0004 decision 2 says the opposite — "Progression is per-Body... Each agent profile carries its own record" — and the ADR's premise is that "the accumulated investment in a Body is real, currently invisible, and worth showing." A record that shrinks when the log is pruned is not a record. "What was true then" is the wargame's own definition of the C case, and C is also what ADR-0004 decision 2 already describes. Rule it here rather than leaving it to whoever writes the first prune.

(2) THE B BRANCH. Rule: "Hot-path cost with a nameable invalidation owner: B", and the "It depends on" warns that "a cache without an owner is a slow bug." config-cache.ts is a 15s-TTL cache of the parsed ~/.hermes/config.yaml keyed in the meta table. `invalidateConfigCache` has exactly one caller in the entire repo: src/app/api/config/route.ts:140. Meanwhile PatterStage itself writes config.yaml from four other functions in src/modules/hermes/lib/config-sync.ts — syncDefaultsToHermesConfig, syncSingleModelToHermesConfig, syncFallbacksToHermesConfig and finalizeRootConfigOnDisk, all via atomicWriteFile — reached from /api/models, /api/models/[id], /api/models/sync/push and /api/models/fallbacks. None invalidates. The walk framed the second writer as "the agent, or a hand edit to ~/.hermes/config.yaml", i.e. as something outside the app's control. It is the app. B is still the right option — the cost is real and the owner is nameable — but it is not met: the TTL is the owner today, which is the slow-bug shape, and the rule's closing line bites: "Never store a derived value that is neither snapshot nor owned cache."
corrections.note: A for stats, C for the per-Body progression snapshot (inputs digest, written before any analytics_events prune), and B for the config read only once every config.yaml writer invalidates — today four in-app writers do not, so the 15s TTL is the owner.
corrections.workImplied: Two small pieces, neither done. (a) Write the per-Body progression snapshot: one row per agent profile carrying level, achievements, the inputs digest and versions, corrections as new rows, and land it BEFORE any analytics_events prune. (b) Call invalidateConfigCache from syncDefaultsToHermesConfig, syncSingleModelToHermesConfig, syncFallbacksToHermesConfig and finalizeRootConfigOnDisk, leaving the 15s TTL as backstop rather than owner.

corrections.originalRuling: C (one language, shared source), needsOwner=true, forked on: "Adopt PatterStudio's tests/fixtures/agentruntime-wire.json as a committed drift gate in this repo, or delete the claim from PatterStudio?"
corrections.correctedRuling: C for the in-repo TypeScript seam, B for every contract that leaves the repo: the JSON Schemas regenerated and diff-gated in CI, and agentruntime-wire.json vendored and asserted as a merge gate. Not a fork — ADR-0002 decision 3 already ordered it, accepted 2026-07-25 and unexecuted. needsOwner: false.
corrections.why:
The decision rule has two branches and this venture sits on both.

IN-REPO. TypeScript on both sides of the app's own seam; components and route handlers import the same type modules; and apiFetch supplies the discipline C owes — src/lib/api-fetch.ts throws a typed ApiError on any non-2xx, which is the "always check response.ok" rule the doctrine names. "One-language monorepo: C is legitimate" holds for this half.

BUT THE SAME SENTENCE CARRIES THE CONDITION, and it is not decoration: "take it with the same commit-and-gate discipline for anything that leaves the repo." Two things leave, and neither is gated. src/lib/schema/json/mission-v1.schema.json and template-pack-v1.schema.json are generated from Zod and committed, and `generate:schema-json` appears in six places, none of them a CI step or a test — its own package.json entry and its own script's header comment. No lint step, no CI job, no test. The committed schema can lag the Zod source silently, which is the failure this wargame says decides the fork. And ADR-0002 decision 1 publishes the node/verdict/outcome/gate and run/agent-event shapes as versioned JSON Schema for TypeScript AND Python to implement — across that seam the venture is two languages, and the first branch is unconditional: "Two languages: B, always, with the generator offline and the schema committed." The generator is already offline and the schemas are already committed; only the gate is missing. The doctrine's closing line is the ruling: "the seam is generated, committed and gated or it lies."

HOW THE ORIGINAL WAS FLATTERY, and it is the subtler kind: C was ruled correctly for the half that costs nothing, and the half that costs work was converted into an owner fork — which parks it. The fork's framing also mis-states the ADR. It argued that adopting the fixture "re-opens the seam ADR-0002 deliberately closed." ADR-0002 closes the RUNTIME dependency (Alternatives rejected: "Consume PatterStack's engine as written... it would make the public product depend on a private repo"). Decision 3 is the opposite of a closure: "PatterStage adopts `agentruntime-wire.json` as a merge gate, closing the convergence gate from its own side without waiting for the other." Status: accepted by Daniel, 2026-07-25. CLAUDE.md is explicit that a decision recorded in docs/adr/ wins over anything inferred from the code. There is nothing for the owner to decide; there is something unbuilt. The cheap form the ADR already implies is vendoring the fixture, which couples nothing at runtime. If the coupling is now judged unacceptable, that is an amendment to ADR-0002 through the ADR process, not a wargame fork.
corrections.note: C in-repo (one language, apiFetch throws on non-2xx), B for everything that leaves it: generate:schema-json runs in no gate anywhere, and ADR-0002 decision 3's agentruntime-wire merge gate is accepted and unbuilt — no owner question remains.
corrections.workImplied: (a) Add a CI step or jest test that regenerates mission-v1.schema.json and template-pack-v1.schema.json and fails on a diff against the committed files — one step, zero coupling. (b) Vendor agentruntime-wire.json into tests/fixtures/ and assert the AgentRuntime port's wire shapes against it, executing ADR-0002 decision 3. Any change of mind on the coupling is an ADR-0002 amendment, not a fork here.

corrections.originalRuling: A. Dark-first, single register (with rec-room's reader as a scoped D exception)
corrections.correctedRuling: A. Dark-first, single register, no exception. The Story Weaver reader's four-theme picker is undeclared option C shipping inside a module: drift under this ruling, not an exception to it.
corrections.why: WG-WEB-001's decision rule has three gates and I walked all three against the facts. (1) "If the brand's identity is luminous or the signature visuals emit light, choose A" — the Cherenkov emission ramp on a #040b12 ground fires this, so A is produced. (2) "Choose C only with a demonstrated dual-context audience" — one operator, one desktop console, local-first; no dual-context audience exists, so C's gate fails. (3) "Consider D when long reads dominate AND the print siblings are light AND the team accepts the second register's QC cost" — all three fail: this same walk rules 27 of 27 routes app shell (WG-WEB-002), there are no print siblings, and the walk's own conflict text says the second QC surface was one "nobody budgeted for". So neither C nor D is reachable and A is unqualified. Now the artefact: ReaderSettings.tsx:11 declares pageTheme: "dark"|"black"|"sepia"|"light"; :30-35 hardcodes four palettes as raw hex including a full light ground (bg #f5f0e8 / text #2c2c2c / accent #7c3aed); :138-148 renders a user-facing four-up picker; :57 persists the choice to localStorage; story-weaver/[id]/page.tsx:306 applies it and :582,:645 add two more conditional hexes (#d4ccc0, #2a2520). By the wargame's own definitions that is C, "Dual register (theme switch): User choice", not D, which is a fixed design decision with no switch. THE FLATTERY, exactly. The argued line asserts "there is no prefers-color-scheme block, data-theme hook or theme toggle anywhere in src/, so the register is already single". I verified the first two (grep returns nothing) — but a theme toggle needs neither mechanism to be a theme toggle, and this one is React state plus localStorage. So the premise is false, and the ruling then takes the very artefact that disproves it and re-labels it a "scoped D exception": wrong option letter, and an exception granted on a condition ("the team accepts the second register's QC cost") the same ruling's conflict paragraph records as never given. Net implied work: zero. Two further checks close it. ADR-0003: "PatterStage stops minting design tokens immediately. Any new token is a change to the shared kit, not to globals.css" — and the kit has no light ground to vendor (PatterStudio/shared/ui theme.css declares --color-void #05080d and --color-surface #0b121b only), so the exception cannot be sourced from the mandated kit and cannot be minted locally. And design-lint.baseline.json already classifies these palettes as debt, not design: no-raw-colour-in-tsx::ReaderSettings.tsx = 4, plus 4 more on the reader page. A shrink-only baseline entry is the repo saying "this is owed"; blessing it as an exception would make it permanent.
corrections.note: A, dark-first, single register, no exception; the Story Weaver reader's four-theme picker is option C drift and comes out.
corrections.workImplied: Delete the `light` and `sepia` entries from THEMES in src/modules/rec-room/components/ReaderSettings.tsx:29-34 and their picker tiles; hold `dark`/`black` on the Cherenkov ladder as tokens rather than hex; remove the two `pageTheme === "light"` conditional hexes at src/app/recroom/story-weaver/[id]/page.tsx:582 and :645. Shrinks the no-raw-colour-in-tsx baseline by up to 8. If the owner wants a light reading register anyway, that is a fork requiring a dated deviation, a budgeted second QC surface, and the palettes minted in @pattertech/ui — never in globals.css or a module.

corrections.originalRuling: B, rich hover treatments only; C deferred until the vendored kit ships it
corrections.correctedRuling: C. Field-reactive, with B's hover treatments as its base layer, delivered by vendoring BloomField from PatterTech_Website into src/kit/ under ADR-0003 Part 1's copy-in model.
corrections.why: The decision rule's first sentence is the operative one: "If the brand's philosophy includes responsiveness or field physics, choose C with B's treatments as its base layer. That clause is brand physics, not house habit." The walk conceded the clause fires ("The brand genuinely IS field physics") and then ruled B, so the whole ruling rests on the two escape clauses. Both fail on inspection. Escape clause one: "Choose B when the team cannot own a shared listener's upkeep." The listener does not need to be owned, it needs to be copied — PatterTech_Website/src/components/ui/BloomField.tsx is 66 lines (I read it): one delegated pointermove plus pointerleave, rAF-throttled, matchMedia gates for (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) and prefers-reduced-motion, returns null. It is finished, shipping in production on the estate's other Cherenkov surface. That is not upkeep a sole dev cannot own; it is the cheapest tier in the whole light system. Escape clause two: "or the audience skews formal" — an instrument console for its own author does not skew formal. Neither fires, so the rule produces C. The ADR-0003 justification does not survive either. Its operative sentence is "PatterStage stops minting design tokens immediately. Any new token is a change to the shared kit, not to globals.css" — tokens, not components; the walk broadened it to "design primitives" to reach B. And I checked the paint rule: the website's globals.css bloom is ~26 lines painting radial-gradient(200px circle at var(--bx) var(--by), rgba(51,221,255,0.07)) — that is #33ddff, the Cherenkov brightest glow PatterStage already documents at docs/design-tokens.md:11 as "51, 221, 255". Zero new tokens. Further, ADR-0003 Part 1 IS a copy-in decision ("copied verbatim into src/kit/ with a PROVENANCE.md"), so vendoring BloomField is that ADR's own distribution model rather than a breach of it. The deferral target is empty: grep for BloomField|data-bloom across PatterStudio/shared/ui returns nothing, so "when @pattertech/ui ships a BloomField" is an unbounded wait on unscheduled work — and WG-WEB-005 defers the same bloom tier in the same walk, which is how an option becomes permanent by default. Finally, B is measurably the zero-work option: 471 hover: utilities in TSX and 0 pointermove/onPointerMove/mousemove handlers anywhere in src/. One collision I checked rather than hedged: the console reserves pulse-glow/glow-surface for live/active state (docs/design-tokens.md:57), and bloom at 0.07 alpha under a 0.4s opacity fade sits far below that threshold in the reference implementation, so "glow = running" stays unambiguous. How bright the ambient tiers go remains WG-WEB-005's open fork; it does not change this option letter.
corrections.note: C, field-reactive, with B's hover layer beneath it: vendor BloomField (66 lines) from PatterTech_Website into src/kit/, not a wait on the kit.
corrections.workImplied: Copy PatterTech_Website/src/components/ui/BloomField.tsx verbatim into src/kit/ with a PROVENANCE.md recording source repo and commit (per ADR-0003 Part 1); mount it once in src/app/layout.tsx; port the ~26-line [data-bloom]::after paint rule into globals.css using the existing Cherenkov RGB (51,221,255) so no token is minted; add data-bloom to the ledger rows, panels, cards and buttons WG-WEB-003 rules as the console's containers; keep the fine-pointer and reduced-motion opt-outs exactly as written. Strike the ADR-0003 sentence from the ruling line — it covers tokens, not components.

corrections.originalRuling: Reference-first (tables, ruled lists, anchor-stable headings, minimal theatre), with the dashboard as the single skim-first surface.
corrections.correctedRuling: Reference-first for the 27 operator routes, skim-first on the dashboard, and the mandatory takeaways band on every long read — which today means building it on the deep-research report, plus anchor-stable heading ids and a navigator at four or more sections. The story reader's commit-decision layer already exists at the library hub and needs only its chapter marks carried into the reader body.
corrections.why: The register half of the original is what the decision rule produces and it stands: session shape is many short lookups against ~43 tables of operational record, the arriving reader is "operators looking something up", which the It-depends-on sends to reference-first. The failure is the word "single". WG-WEB-006's decision rule opens unconditionally — "Every long read gets the skim layer anyway (the takeaways band); the fork is how much pacing machinery follows" — and it is not conditioned on the register chosen. "Single" is an adjective the rule does not permit, and it foreclosed the one clause that would have cost work. THE FLATTERY: src/app/page.tsx's own header comment reads "One-glance situational awareness → one-click actions", so naming the dashboard skim-first describes the file rather than ruling on it — implied work, zero. I then checked both long reads that this same walk designated in WG-WEB-002, and the answer differs between them, which is why checking mattered. THE STORY READER IS SUBSTANTIALLY MET, and I would have got this wrong by assuming: library/page.tsx:158-163 already shows chapter count, word count and "~N min read", :189-194 a chapter-progress bar, and the reader mounts ChapterList. That is precisely the form the doctrine's own worked ruling used for a narrative index ("type and reading-time meta so the choice to commit is informed from the hub"). The gap there is small: the marks live in the hub and the sidebar, not in the reading body. THE RESEARCH REPORT HAS NOTHING. ResearchReport.tsx:43 defines one PROSE constant applied at :97 via dangerouslySetInnerHTML with no band above it; grep for "In brief"/takeaway across src/components/research and src/app/laboratory returns nothing. And a fact the audit did not have: renderReportHtml at src/lib/laboratory/deep-research/markdown.ts:78 emits bare <h1>-<h6> with no id attribute, so the headings are not anchor-stable and the navigator the rule's "four or more chapters" clause requires cannot be built without changing the renderer — the same absence also defeats the "anchor-stable headings" the reference-first register itself names. The rule's last clause bites too: the brief records "both, equally", and its answer is not lower density but "structure so the headings, takeaways and plaques alone carry the argument while the prose carries the depth" — a structural obligation, not a copy edit. Density is currently bought the wrong way and the repo says so: no-sub-12px-type is 370 of the 869 baselined violations (the other 449 are docs em-dashes), i.e. the largest live category, against a rule whose own text says sub-12px "is unreadable at arm's length".

corrections.workImplied: Require the synthesize step to emit a leading `## In brief` of 3-5 bullets and render it as a band above PROSE in src/components/research/ResearchReport.tsx; add slugged id attributes to the heading branch of renderReportHtml (src/lib/laboratory/deep-research/markdown.ts:78) and mirror them in the standalone HTML export; render an on-page navigator when a report carries four or more h2s; carry ChapterList's marks into the story reader's body. corrections.originalRuling: A, media is a citation in the reading column (mode: inherited)
corrections.correctedRuling: A, argued, with docs/ in scope: media is a citation in the reading column, which the venture's seven shipped screenshots do not yet satisfy — no captions, no reading measure on two of three longform surfaces, and one uncited image.
corrections.why: First, the mode. Four triggers name this wargame (tags: web, media, layout, content) and `web` is recorded in VENTURE_BRIEF as present, so WALK_ORDER's rule leaves no room: a wargame a trigger names must be argued. Second, the premise the inheritance rested on. "There is no media" is true of src/ and false of the venture: git ls-files returns seven tracked PNGs in docs/images/ totalling 688 KB, embedded at README.md:9 and at USER_WALKTHROUGH_GUIDE.md:69,156,276,323,381,736 — the venture's two longest shipped documents, and both B product surfaces under this walk's own WG-VOX-001. The premise held only because the search was scoped to a directory where the answer was guaranteed. Now the decision rule, against the corrected facts. (1) "What the piece treats the media as": in USER_WALKTHROUGH_GUIDE each screenshot heads the section it documents — cited evidence, A's case. README.md:9 sits under the intro as a hero shot — monument in intent. (2) "Content or pacing": all seven are the venture's own screenshots, content, never tonal bands. (3) "Whether the layout guarantees that a bleed means the same width in every wrapper": GitHub's markdown renderer offers no bleed mechanism, so B is structurally unavailable on the surfaces where this venture's media actually lives; in-app I confirmed both renderers escape HTML first and implement no image syntax, and the only w-screen hits in src/ are max-w-screen-xl container caps at missions/page.tsx:214,238. (4) The rule itself is unconditional: "Media is a citation... If a block contains an image, a video or an iframe, it does not get a band." So A, and now argued rather than assumed. A IS NOT FREE, which is the point of arguing it. Option A's own text defines a citation as "a figure with a caption"; zero of the seven carry one — alt text is a label for assistive tech, not a caption, and "![PatterStage dashboard]" tells a reader nothing the heading above it did not. "In the reading column" presupposes a measure, and the venture holds one on one of three longform surfaces: ResearchReport.tsx:43's PROSE sets no max-width, artifacts/page.tsx:160 is `prose max-w-none`, only story-weaver/[id]/page.tsx:580 has max-w-3xl. And docs/images/insights.png (88 KB, fifth of seven by size) is referenced by no document at all — its only hit anywhere is tests/e2e/screenshots.spec.ts:24, the script that generates it. An image cited by nothing is not a citation; it is weight. Which lands on death #1: install.sh:258 clones with no --depth, so all 688 KB ships to every stranger. WG-WEB-012 raised exactly this as a hypothetical ("a contributor could add a public/ directory of screenshots with a fully green build"); it has already happened, in docs/. Worth recording for the estate: PatterTech Website ruled A at scale S, PatterStage now rules A argued at scale M, which is the second concordant ruling and the second venture scale that GOVERNANCE.md's promotion arithmetic was missing.
corrections.note: A, argued not inherited: media is a citation — and the seven shipped screenshots in docs/ owe captions, a measure, and the deletion of the uncited one.
corrections.workImplied: Add a one-line caption under each of the seven figures in README.md and docs/USER_WALKTHROUGH_GUIDE.md naming what the shot shows; delete docs/images/insights.png or cite it (it is generated by tests/e2e/screenshots.spec.ts:24 and referenced by no document); set a reading measure on the two longform surfaces that lack one — a max-width on ResearchReport.tsx:43's PROSE and on artifacts/page.tsx:160's `prose max-w-none` — so "in the reading column" is enforceable before the first in-app figure exists. Correct the "only binary asset is favicon.ico" premise in the WG-WEB-008 and WG-WEB-012 notes and record 688 KB as a clone-weight fact under death #1.

corrections.originalRuling: C — mixed, but inverted: the stateful app ships as a native host install, the container is the CI parity rig. Forked (needsOwner) on whether a stranger gets a third deployment model.
corrections.correctedRuling: A. One deployment model, and it is the native host install. The artefact CI proves must be the artefact a stranger receives, so PRs gate on scripts/bootstrap/install.sh end to end on a clean machine, and the container stops being a second shipped model (retired from DEPLOY.md's supported set and from the PR-required checks, or kept only as an unsupported convenience carrying no gate). A's OCI form is deviated, not blessed: the one model is a native install rather than an image because the app's job is to drive the host, and the deviation carries A's parity obligation intact rather than excusing it.
corrections.why:
Walk the decision rule's three clauses against the venture. Clause 1: "Handover or parity clauses in force, or a cloud estate ruled by WG-OPS-001: A, one model, local harness running the same images." The second disjunct is false (WG-OPS-001 ruled C, self-hosting; there is no cloud estate). The first is true, and the walk itself says so: "The parity trigger the wargame uses to force A does fire, and hard, because every install is a handover to unseen hardware." The brief makes that handover the gate on the whole venture — nothing else integrates until "one person who is not the author has installed it from scratch and used it for a week." Clause 2 (PaaS-hosted with static-export fronts → C) fails on both terms: PatterTech hosts nothing and there is no static front. Clause 3 (B alone) fails: there is an API. Only clause 1 fires, and it produces A. There is no clause under which C is reachable.

The flattery is the redefinition. C as written is "the API and workers as containers... static and edge fronts on their platform's native build." PatterStage has no static front and its stateful part is not containerised, so nothing in the wargame's C describes this venture. The walk conceded the A trigger fires "and hard", then wrote "C — mixed, but inverted" and admitted in the same paragraph that "the doctrine's C is inverted here and its decision rule's premise fails." Relabelling an option to mean its opposite is not ruling; it is the deployment equivalent of moving a coverage floor down, which is why the audit put it in this lens.

What A honestly costs, stated rather than dodged: A's literal form (every surface an OCI image from one Dockerfile family) is not available here, because the product's function is to drive the host it runs on — ~/.hermes, host git, crontab/schtasks, port kill, ps-deploy restarting the host process. The current Dockerfile already pays for that impersonation (bash, git, curl, iproute2, psmisc, socat installed into the runtime layer per DEPLOY.md) and still cannot run update or rebuild, because .dockerignore excludes .git (confirmed: `.git` is the first line). So A is ruled on its substance — one model, parity by construction, the harness exercising the shipped artefact — with the artefact form recorded as a named deviation and its reason written down. That is not the walk's move: the walk kept two models and renamed the arrangement; this reduces to one and imposes the parity proof the arrangement never had.

The defect A exposes is the inversion in CI, and I re-verified every part of it. ci.yml runs `docker-image` on every pull_request (line 224: docker build + tests/scripts/docker-deploy-api-smoke.sh). `boot-smoke` (line 157) runs only cross-platform primitives with no app build. `real-hermes-integration` is gated `if: github.event_name == 'push' || workflow_dispatch` (line 252). Nothing anywhere in ci.yml runs install.sh. So the artefact nobody ships is proven on every PR and the artefact every stranger receives is proven by nobody — and that artefact is the one carrying cheapest death #1.

The work is smaller than the walk implied, because the harness already exists: tests/integration/test_full_install_update_process.py builds an ephemeral image and runs install.sh (bootstrap clone via a file:// bare repo), install.sh --in-repo, setup.sh and ps-deploy update in throwaway containers. Its own docstring says "Not intended for CI" and docs/TESTING.md:68 repeats "This is not part of CI—run it manually before releases." Under A plus delivery doctrine rule 5, that disclaimer is the thing that changes.

The fork narrows rather than dying, and I am recording the narrowed form instead of the three-option one. A permits exactly one model, so the interview's ".exe" is not a third option to add — it is a candidate to replace install.sh, and choosing it reverses the Linux-first ruling that install.ps1 (a 23-line stub redirecting to WSL2) currently implements. The owner question is which single model, not how many.
corrections.workImplied: Wire the existing install harness into CI as a PR gate (tests/integration/test_full_install_update_process.py --profile smoke --skip-http, or a CI slice of it) and strike its "not intended for CI" disclaimer; demote docker-image out of the PR-required checks and cut DEPLOY.md's supported models to one. Ordered behind WG-DEL-004, because setup.sh:211 runs `npm run build` and that build fetches fonts from the network.

corrections.originalRuling: B (budget with approval gates) with C (hard caps) layered on unattended agent work. needsOwner=false.
corrections.correctedRuling: B and C, split by whose money it is. B for the operator's own install, made real: a monthly figure in the venture's state file, spend logged per session from the estimates model-cost.ts already produces, and triage pausing unattended work when the figure is breached. C layered on unattended work and located where the doctrine puts it — the LLM provider's own console, which does offer a service-stopping monthly ceiling — not built into PatterStage. Because PatterStage ships, the same C binds the user: enabling unattended work must require that a provider ceiling has been set and must show the running total against it. No in-product spend governor is ordered by this ruling.
corrections.why:
Apply the rule clause by clause. "Contract money or any second stakeholder: B... the approver named" — does not fire; the brief records no money trigger, no agreements, a sole operator. "Own money, real workloads: B without the second signature" — fires, because four unattended loops dispatch inference (src/lib/mission-queue-tick.ts, src/lib/composer/scheduler/composer-tick.ts, src/lib/host-scheduler.ts, src/lib/laboratory/deep-research/run-job.ts) and the operator's standing constraint is "No spend without my approval." "A only where the worst month is lunch money" — does not fire; an unattended loop has no bound. "Experiments... and anything an unattended fleet can scale: C where the platform offers it, on top of B" — the fleet trigger fires.

On F10 I part-agree and part-disagree, and the disagreement matters. F10 says C's clause is empty because WG-OPS-001 ruled self-hosting so "there is no platform to offer a ceiling." I do not accept that reading: the wargame's own question text says the fork "applies to agent spend as much as to hosting," and the platform that meters agent spend is the LLM provider, not the host. A provider console's monthly usage limit is C verbatim — "platform-enforced ceilings that stop service rather than overspend." So C's clause is not empty; it points outside this repo, at whoever holds the API key. What F10 gets exactly right is the consequence of leaving C unlocated: an unlocated hard cap silently becomes a product build, on the sole dev whose death #2 is the budget going to seams. Locating it is the fix, and it costs a documented precondition and an enable-time check rather than a spend governor.

The letters therefore survive, but the walk made neither half true and hid a second money-holder behind needsOwner=false. PatterStage today is A with a dashboard, and I re-verified it: there is no org/ directory in this repo at all, and zero hits across src/ and docs/ for spendCap, monthlyBudget, spend_limit, maxSpend, costCeiling or spendLimit. Every `budget` identifier is a time or round budget (hindsight reflect budget in api/memory/hindsight/route.ts, deep-research's round budget, llm.ts's retry budget, SyncScheduler's staleness budget). The only cost_usd column is in 014_benchmarks.sql, the subsystem ADR-0004 records as deleted. The reporting half exists and works (model-cost.ts estimateCost → run-aggregates.ts:120 costUsd → the Insights total); the governing half is absent. A is unreachable under the rule, so this gap is work, not a footnote.

Two venture facts the doctrine's "whose money is it" axis does not carry, ruled rather than deferred. First, llm-endpoint.ts makes local OpenAI-compatible endpoints a first-class path, so a genuine zero-spend configuration exists; that is what makes C a settable precondition on paid providers rather than a universal obligation to build a ceiling. Second, PatterStage ships, so an unattended loop can spend a stranger's money. B's mechanism — a figure in the operator's state file — cannot reach that person; C's can, because it is set at their own provider. That split is what dissolves the fork F10 proposes: the clause "where the platform offers it" answers it, and the answer costs the venture no build.

Finally the rule's tail: "Tier cliffs are design inputs... belong in the architecture rulings (WG-ARCH-008)." PatterStage's equivalent knobs — deep-research's round budget, context size, retry budget — are all tuned for latency today and none is read as a cost knob. Under C on top of B, the round budget is the venture's own ceiling and has to be read that way.
corrections.workImplied: Write the monthly figure and the spend rule into the venture's state file (no org/ exists in this repo yet); display the run-aggregates spend total against that figure; add a triage pause that stops unattended dispatch once it is breached. For shipped installs, make a provider ceiling a documented precondition of enabling unattended work and surface the running total at that point. Re-label deep-research's round budget as a cost knob.

corrections.originalRuling: B. Floors per surface, ratchet-only-up, set from today's honest measurement, not from the current placeholder numbers.
corrections.correctedRuling: B, with the two clauses the original left out. Three bands, not two — engine (src/lib/runtime), service (the API route handlers), UI (src/components) — which requires deleting "!src/app/**" from collectCoverageFrom, because a surface that is not measured cannot carry a floor. And the ratchet is a machine, not a convention: the shrink-only mechanism this repo already runs for design-lint must own the coverage floors, since jest.config.js is a file anyone can edit downwards and this venture has already done so once.
corrections.why:
The decision rule is short and the letter is not in doubt: "CI exists: B... A only where there is no CI (S ventures); C never." CI exists — build-test-ubuntu and build-test-macos both run `npm run test:coverage`. B is the only reachable letter, and the original's headline (floors set from honest measurement, not the placeholder numbers) is right and stands.

The flattery is in the note, not the letter, and it is the subtle kind this pass exists to catch: "which is already the doctrine's engine-above-service-above-UI ordering." That asserts a three-term ordering on two terms. jest.config.js line 22 is "!src/app/**", so every API route handler is excluded from measurement outright, along with all page.tsx and layout.tsx. The service band — the middle term of the doctrine's ordering, and in this venture the surface holding the single authentication enforcement point and the subsystem that most recently failed (the Phase S1 unauthenticated-RCE fix) — produces no number and therefore cannot be assigned a floor. Two measured numbers happening to sort correctly is not the rule being met; the rule names three surfaces and one of them is invisible. Ruling B without naming that hole grades the venture on a band it does not measure.

Second, "never lower one without a ruled deviation" is a mechanism requirement, not a piece of history. I verified 0e3fef9b: branches 5→4, lines 5→4, statements 5→4, commit body "Lowered thresholds to 4% ... to unblock CI." The values have since recovered (today 10/8/5/10 global and 15/12/8/15 for src/lib, restored by 03384ccd and later work), which is exactly why the original could file it under conflict and move on. But nothing changed to stop the next lowering: the floors live in an editable config and CLAUDE.md's prohibition is a sentence, not a gate. Delivery doctrine rule 2 says ratchets "move upwards in the change that earned the movement, and never down without a ruled deviation"; rule 6 says a red gate is never negotiated. The repo already operates the correct machine for precisely this — design-lint.baseline.json is per-file and shrink-only, guarded by the string at scripts/tooling/design-lint.mjs:246, "Do NOT run --update-baseline to silence a new violation; the baseline only shrinks," repeated at docs/REPO_GUIDE.md:27. Ruling B while leaving coverage outside that machine leaves the one gate this venture has already proven it will negotiate.

Third, the part the original did say and which survives: a global floor of 10 against a measured ~54.7% is not a floor, it is decoration — no regression a human would notice can trip it.
corrections.workImplied: Delete "!src/app/**" from collectCoverageFrom and add a src/app/api band; reset every floor to the measured number rounded down (engine above service above UI); move the floors into a shrink-only baseline checked by the same mechanism as design-lint.baseline.json, so a downward edit fails CI instead of passing it.

corrections.originalRuling: B. Fast suites gate every change; the full end-to-end acceptance suite, including the install journey, blocks main. Note: "only wiring separates PatterStage from B."
corrections.correctedRuling: B, letter unchanged, premise struck. "Only wiring" is false: today's arrangement is not a tier, it is a single smoke gate — PLAYWRIGHT_SMOKE=1 leaves 38 of 42 tests and 12 of 13 spec files running on no branch in CI at all. B requires three things this venture does not have: the full suite running as a main-blocking job with PLAYWRIGHT_SMOKE off; real-hermes-integration moved from push-only into the PR-blocking set for main, because proving after the merge inverts "the trunk takes assembled proof"; and acceptance journeys actually written, since the existing specs are render assertions. The install journey stays in the blocking set and is now determined rather than hostage: WG-OPS-002 rules A, one model, the native install, and the harness already exists.
corrections.why:
Decision rule: "A real local stack and synthetic external modes exist: B, with the acceptance journeys... encoded in the blocking set. No harness yet: A, and building the harness is the standing foundation order." Both preconditions hold and I checked them: mock-hermes/, mock-llm/ and mock-hindsight/ exist at the repo root with their own servers (two with Dockerfiles), and playwright.config.ts boots a real production `npm run start` against an isolated CH_DATA_DIR that global-setup wipes. So B is what the rule produces and the letter is right.

The flattery is the sentence "so only wiring separates PatterStage from B," and it is contradicted by the ruling's own next paragraph ("Encoding B means writing the acceptance journeys, not just lifting PLAYWRIGHT_SMOKE") and by the count. I counted the suite directly: 42 tests across 13 spec files; smoke.spec.ts holds 4; so 38 tests and 12 files run on no branch — not on PRs, not on dev, not on main. docs/TESTING.md:60 states it without varnish: "CI does not run the full matrix on every push," with the remedy being a human instruction to run it locally before a dev→main merge. That is neither tier of B; it is one gate of four assertions with a habit behind it. Delivery doctrine rule 5 binds independently of the letter: "Fast suites gate every change; the end-to-end acceptance journeys block main." Calling that distance "wiring" is the same move as calling a floor of 10 a floor.

On F8, which held that this ruling's install clause was hostage to the WG-OPS-002 fork: that is no longer true, and it is why these two corrections belong in one pass. WG-OPS-002 now rules A — one model, the native install — so the journey's content is determined. It is also already written: tests/integration/test_full_install_update_process.py exercises install.sh, install.sh --in-repo, setup.sh and ps-deploy update in throwaway containers; it merely disclaims CI in its own docstring, echoed at TESTING.md:68. So the install half of B is genuinely a wiring job — the one place the phrase applies, and the original applied it to the half where it does not.

One real ordering constraint, recorded as a sequence rather than used as an escape: the install journey cannot run deterministically in CI until WG-DEL-004's fix lands, because setup.sh:211 runs `npm run build` and that build fetches six Google Font families over the network. DEL-004 is ruled C and comes first.
corrections.workImplied: Add a main-blocking job that runs the full Playwright suite with PLAYWRIGHT_SMOKE unset; change real-hermes-integration's `if:` so it also runs on pull_request targeting main; wire the install harness in as the install journey once WG-DEL-004 lands; convert the render-assertion specs into journeys, starting with missions-runtime.spec.ts, which says so in its own header.

corrections.originalRuling: B. Component states, pixel-exact, zero threshold, pinned container, baselines committed. FORKED (needsOwner): cut the first baselines against today's src/components/ui, or wait until ADR-0003 vendors @pattertech/ui into src/kit/?
corrections.correctedRuling: B, and the fork is withdrawn: the first baselines are cut against the kit that exists today. The decision rule conditions B on "a component kit exists", not on which kit, and states that A is tolerable "only before any kit exists". src/components/ui holds 24 primitives plus a field kit; src/kit does not exist on disk. Waiting is taking A behind an accepted, unexecuted ADR for an unbounded period, which is the exact failure this wargame names. Re-baselining when the vendored kit lands is a reviewed event, which B already provides for.
corrections.why:
Decision rule, first clause: "A component kit exists: B, from the kit's first week, in the pinned container the stack profile specifies." I verified the kit — src/components/ui holds 24 primitives plus a field/ directory, 25 entries in all — so B applies and its start date is long past. The last clause is what kills the fork: "A is tolerable only before any kit exists, and building the styleguide surface ends it." A kit exists, so A is not tolerable, and deferring the first baselines is taking A whatever it is called.

I checked the deferral target: `ls src/kit` returns no such file or directory, and ADR-0003 is accepted and unexecuted. This walk was caught making the identical move twice elsewhere — SQ-05 deferring the bloom tier to a BloomField that exists in no target repo, and F1-arch005 treating an accepted ADR's order as a closed door — so I will not repeat it here. "When the vendored kit lands" is not a date. The fork's own text named the mechanism it then chose to run: waiting "makes the VRT gate hostage to an ADR that is accepted and unexecuted, which is exactly the mechanism by which option A persists indefinitely." The cost of not waiting is one re-baseline, which B classifies as a reviewed event rather than a breach; the cost of waiting is unbounded.

The remaining conditions are work, not obstacles, and the original was right that they are large. There is no visual gate of any kind: I re-grepped the tree and found zero hits for toHaveScreenshot, toMatchSnapshot, Storybook, Lost Pixel, Percy or Chromatic outside the walk file itself. There is no styleguide surface enumerating component states, and the doctrine says building it is what ends A. The only screenshot machinery, tests/e2e/screenshots.spec.ts, is opt-in doc-image capture — fullPage shots after a bare waitForTimeout(1500) with no comparison — which is the non-deterministic shape this wargame names as how the gate goes soft.

One interaction on the record so it is not later misread as an exception. B requires a pinned render container, and WG-OPS-002 was just ruled A with the container retired as a deployment model. These do not collide: B's container is a render rig, not a deploy artefact, and the doctrine's own WiseWattage ruling used exactly that ("rendered in the pinned Docker image after host fonts made identical code diff across machines"). Retiring Docker as a shipped model does not retire it as a test rig; that is the role in which it earns its keep. Separately, F9's collision lands here and costs one flag: committed baselines add binary weight to a repo whose install path clones with --single-branch and no --depth, so the stranger pays the full history at install.
corrections.workImplied: Build the styleguide surface enumerating the 24 primitives' states; add a pinned render container and zero-threshold comparison over those states with committed baselines; add --depth 1 to install.sh's clone so baseline history is not paid at install time.

corrections.originalRuling: C. Determinism first, zero retries on blocking gates, with B (quarantine plus a filed order and a deadline) as the only containment valve.
corrections.correctedRuling: C, unchanged — the one ruling in this cluster the decision rule confirms as written. One clause added, on ordering rather than substance: retries must reach 0 in playwright.config.ts BEFORE WG-DEL-002 un-smokes the suite, and the fonts must be local before any install job can gate a PR; otherwise the venture converts a retry-tolerant gate of 4 tests into a retry-tolerant gate of 42, and the two install-gating rulings inherit a build that needs the network.
corrections.why:
The decision rule states the posture unconditionally: "C is the posture: build the determinism budget in... and keep retries at zero on blocking gates. When a flake cannot be root-caused this week, B contains it: quarantine, order, deadline, never silence. A is forbidden on blocking gates; a scheduled job may retry, a gate may not." The default repeats it. No venture fact reaches another letter, and I could find no way this ruling flatters anything: it is the hardest option in the wargame, the code fails it in five places, and every one of those still holds on inspection. Recording it unchanged is a result, not a pass.

Re-verified: playwright.config.ts:15 sets `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0` and :25 sets `trace: "on-first-retry"` — an automatic retry on a gate that runs on every pull_request, which is the forbidden A, with the retry designed in as the debugging path rather than tolerated as an accident. Around it ci.yml stacks four more: a `continue-on-error` checkout plus a duplicate retry step (repeated across six jobs), `npm ci || (npm cache clean --force && npm ci)`, a three-attempt curl warmup of six fonts.googleapis.com URLs at :120-139, and `npm run build || (sleep 5; npm run build)` at :147-152 whose own comment names the known flake it exists to survive. Delivery doctrine rule 4 is the binding form ("blocking gates run zero retries") and rule 6 forbids negotiating a red gate.

The part that makes this more than CI hygiene stands too, and two other corrections in this pass now depend on it. scripts/bootstrap/setup.sh:211 runs `npm run build` on the stranger's machine; six next/font/google families are fetched at build time across src/app/layout.tsx and src/app/recroom/story-weaver/layout.tsx; there is no public/fonts and no local fallback. A stranger without egress to fonts.googleapis.com gets a hard build failure — cheapest death #3 and the determinism debt are one defect, currently disguised as a flaky macOS job. WG-OPS-002's install-gating CI job and WG-DEL-002's install journey both run that build, so neither can be deterministic until this lands. That makes C the first item in the cluster's order, not the last.
corrections.workImplied: Set Playwright retries to 0 unconditionally and switch trace to retain-on-failure; vendor the six font families as local .woff2 under next/font/local and delete both the font warmup and the build retry from ci.yml; drop the npm ci and checkout retries, or file each as a quarantined flake with an order and a deadline. Do this before the other three delivery items.

resolutions.conflict: Whether adopting PatterStudio's tests/fixtures/agentruntime-wire.json is still an open question. The walk's fork asked "adopt it as a committed drift gate, or delete the claim from PatterStudio?" and argued that adopting "re-opens the seam ADR-0002 deliberately closed". ADR-0002 does not close that seam; decision 3 orders the adoption.
resolutions.resolution: ADR-0002 wins and the fork is WITHDRAWN. I read the ADR myself (docs/adr/0002-run-engine-ownership.md). What it closes is the RUNTIME dependency — Alternatives rejected: "Consume PatterStack's engine as written… it would make the public product depend on a private repo." Decision 3 is the opposite of a closure: "PatterStage adopts `agentruntime-wire.json` as a merge gate, closing the convergence gate from its own side without waiting for the other." resolutions.conflict: Whether PatterStage has a brand family to map. resolutions.resolution: Re-rule as A, one accent. This is not a pair where one ruling loses to another so much as a ruling whose own evidence sends it elsewhere, and all three branches agree. (1) The decision rule: "No family at all (one trade, one brand) → A with a single accent; the map is overhead without imprints", and "Purely topical sections → A". B requires "sub-brands with independent identity and published work". I read src/lib/modules/registry.ts: the four entries are titled Console (core), Operations (hermes), Laboratory and Rec Room — sections of one application. ADR-0001 forbids the thing that would make them imprints: "a product appears as a row with liveness and an outbound link, never as a nested tree of its pages." ADR-0005's module seam is an internal import boundary, not a brand family. (2) The named source has no map in it: PatterStudio/shared/ui/src/theme.css declares one single-hue Cherenkov ramp (#33ddff, #00bfff, #00a1e6, #008bd1, #0071c2), one --color-amber, and three semantic tokens (ok/warn/danger). Minting four decorative accents locally is precisely what ADR-0003 forbids ("PatterStage stops minting design tokens immediately"). (3) B's own contrast clause fails independently. I recomputed the ratios rather than quoting them: --color-neon-purple #8b5cff (globals.css:16) is 4.44:1 on --color-dark-900 #0c1520 and 4.03:1 on --color-dark-800 #121f2d, both under the 4.5:1 body minimum — and purple is the accent proposed to carry two of the four modules. The Cherenkov head #33ddff measures 11.3:1 and 10.26:1 on the same two grounds, so A is also the accessible answer.
resolutions.losingRuling: WG-WEB-009 becomes A, argued: one Cherenkov accent for the whole console, semantic colours (ok/warn/danger) reserved for state, module identity carried by structure and label rather than hue. This dissolves the five-competing-accents defect the walk found — a single sidebar flying purple, green, cyan, orange and pink — instead of formalising it into a registered map. A module-colour family remains available only as a fork, and that fork requires accents minted in @pattertech/ui as an estate decision; it can never be minted in globals.css.
resolutions.workImplied: Delete the per-link `color:` string literals from src/lib/modules/registry.ts (36+ sites across the four modules), retire the neon-* set to semantic use only, and re-point the components that consume the accent at the Cherenkov ramp. resolutions.conflict: The status of the bloom tier, and whether ADR-0003 bars building light primitives locally. The fork survives narrowed and re-posed: not WHICH tiers, but the dimmer height WITHIN C — v3's ≥18s conduit duty cycles versus v4's ≥12s plus the one-shot heading sweep — on a 27-route operator console. The "day of CSS versus an estate decision" framing is withdrawn; verified that globals.css today has zero radial-gradient fields and zero conduits, and that ps-rail-flow (0.5s linear infinite) is a live-state signal on one component in ResearchReport.tsx, not an ambient conduit, so it neither satisfies the tier nor breaches the duty-cycle budget.

resolutions.conflict: Whether analytics_events may be pruned. WG-ARCH-003 ruled A (always computed) on the ground that "nothing here carries attestation weight", while the progression record is derived live from analytics_events; WG-ARCH-008's retention obligation lands on that same table. Execute the prune and the operator's level drops and earned achievements un-earn.
resolutions.resolution: Both rulings stand as corrected, and the collision is ruled here rather than left to whoever writes the first prune. Same module, so ownership splits by subject: WG-ARCH-003 owns whether a derived value is a snapshot, an owned cache or always computed; WG-ARCH-008 owns topology and retention. ARCH-003's C is taken for the per-Body progression record — an immutable per-profile snapshot carrying its inputs digest — because that is the one point-in-time fact in the system, and ARCH-003's rule names this case exactly ("Point-in-time legal or attestation weight: C, and the snapshot records its inputs so it can be re-derived and audited"). ARCH-008 keeps its retention obligation intact. Until a joint wargame exists the stricter rule applies, and here it takes the form of an ordering: the snapshot lands BEFORE any prune. No retention exemption is granted — an unbounded append-only table on a machine meant to run for years, and on machines belonging to people the operator has never met, is not a loss he can accept on their behalf. Verified: 011_drop_game_tables.sql records progression as "derived live from real activity in the stats layer"; derive.ts:314 computes `unlocked: current >= def.target` on every read; analytics-repository's distinctActiveDays() and distinctEventTypeCount() scan the whole table with no time bound; the only DELETE-for-age anywhere in the app is LogSync.ts:169 keeping 500 error_log_entries. ADR-0004 decision 2 already describes the snapshot: "Progression is per-Body… Each agent profile carries its own record."
resolutions.losingRuling: Neither loses its letter. WG-ARCH-003's blanket A is narrowed — A for stats generally, C for the per-Body progression record, and B for the config read only once its invalidation owner is complete — and its note "this is the one wargame PatterStage already answers to spec" is struck. WG-ARCH-008 gains a sequencing constraint rather than an exemption: its retention plan for analytics_events and chat_messages is owed, and the prune it orders is blocked until the snapshot exists. A record that shrinks when the log is pruned is not a record.
resolutions.workImplied: Write the per-Body progression snapshot first: one row per agent profile carrying level, achievements, the inputs digest and versions, corrections as new rows. Then, and only then, the prune — with consumer, retention window, prune path and the physical-split migration written into the migration headers and an ADR for both analytics_events and chat_messages.

resolutions.conflict: Whether a platform exists to offer a hard ceiling. WG-OPS-001 ruled C (self-hosting) and states in its own conflict that "PatterStage's runtime cost and pager transfer wholesale to the user, so there is no account, no region, no root holder". WG-OPS-004 layered C (hard caps) on unattended agent work, whose clause reads "C where the platform offers it" — which the audit reads as empty, silently converting a platform setting into an unbudgeted product build.
resolutions.resolution: Both rulings stand; the clause is not empty, it points OUTSIDE this repo. Same module, so the wargame's own text decides rather than a precedence tiebreak: WG-OPS-004's question says the fork "applies to agent spend as much as to hosting", and the platform that meters agent spend is the LLM provider, not the host. A provider console's monthly usage limit is C verbatim — a platform-enforced ceiling that stops service rather than overspending. So WG-OPS-001's ruling empties the HOSTING half of the clause and leaves the AGENT-SPEND half intact. The ordering cycle the audit found is broken by scope, not by preference: OPS-001 answers where it runs and is the input to OPS-004's C clause, so hosting is ruled first; OPS-004 answers what governs spend, which is what OPS-001's own rule defers to it. The audit's substantive warning is upheld in full: an unlocated hard cap silently becomes a product build on the sole dev whose death #2 is the budget going to seams. Locating it at the provider is the fix, and it costs a documented precondition plus an enable-time check rather than a spend governor.
resolutions.losingRuling: WG-OPS-004's blanket "C layered on unattended agent work" is restated, split by whose money it is, so it no longer implies an in-product ceiling. B for the operator's own install, made real: a monthly figure in the venture's state file, spend logged per session from the estimates model-cost.ts already produces, and triage pausing unattended dispatch once the figure is breached. C for the stranger, located at their own provider: enabling unattended work must require that a provider ceiling has been set and must show the running total against it. No in-product spend governor is ordered. needsOwner stays false — the fork the audit proposed dissolves on the clause "where the platform offers it", and src/lib/llm-endpoint.ts's local OpenAI-compatible path is what makes the precondition settable rather than a universal obligation. What does not survive is the claim that today's arrangement is B: verified zero hits across src/ and docs/ for spendCap, monthlyBudget, spend_limit, maxSpend, costCeiling or spendLimit, no org/ directory in this repo at all, and every `budget` identifier is a time or round budget. PatterStage is A with a dashboard.
resolutions.workImplied: Write the monthly figure and the spend rule into the venture's state file; display the run-aggregates spend total against it; add a triage pause that stops unattended dispatch once breached. For shipped installs, make a provider ceiling a documented precondition of enabling unattended work and surface the running total at that point. Re-label deep-research's round budget as a cost knob, per the rule's tail sending tier-cliff decisions to WG-ARCH-008.
